steps.title: Optimize Sample Concentration and Absorbance
steps.instruction: Ensure sample concentration and absorbance are within the required range for reproducible results.

substeps.instruction: Adjust sample concentration using Sample Buffer or an Amicon centrifuge concentrator (10,000 MWCO) so that the absorbance decrease is between 0.02 and 0.135/min.
Dilute samples with Sample Buffer if the initial absorbance at 340 nm is > 1.2 (e.g., erythrocyte lysates).

If samples contain high levels of GSSG or NADPH consuming enzymes, remove GSSG via dialysis or gel filtration column, or perform a blank without cumene hydroperoxide to assess non-specific oxidation of NADPH.

steps.title: Initiate the Reaction
steps.instruction: Start the enzymatic reaction across all used wells.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µl of Cumene Hydroperoxide to all wells as quickly as possible.
Record the precise time the reaction was initiated.
Carefully shake the plate for a few seconds to mix.

steps.title: Measure Absorbance
steps.instruction: Monitor the reaction using a plate reader.

substeps.instruction: Read the absorbance at 340 nm once every minute.
Verify that the initial absorbance of sample wells is between 0.5 and 1.2.

steps.title: Calculate GPx Activity
steps.instruction: Determine the enzyme activity based on the change in absorbance.

substeps.instruction: Determine the change in absorbance (ΔA 340) per minute by plotting absorbance values vs. time to find the slope of the linear portion, or by calculating the change between two points on the linear portion (using absolute values).
Subtract the ΔA 340/min rate of the background/non-enzymatic wells from the sample well rates.
Calculate GPx activity using the NADPH extinction coefficient of 0.00373 µM⁻¹ (adjusted for a 0.6 cm pathlength from the actual coefficient of 0.00622 µM⁻¹cm⁻¹).
Define one unit as the amount of enzyme causing the oxidation of 1.0 nmol of NADPH to NADP+ per minute at 25 ºC.

description: Background or Non-enzymatic Wells - add 120 µl of Assay Buffer and 50 µl of co-substrate mixture to three wells.
